title: Resident Evil Requiem [Switch 2]
description:
Resident Evil Requiem is the ninth mainline entry in Capcom's Resident Evil series and a single-player survival-horror/action game for Nintendo Switch 2.

The story follows two intertwined protagonists. Grace Ashcroft is an FBI analyst whose investigation is closely tied to a disturbing abandoned hotel and to the death of her mother. Her sections emphasise vulnerability, exploration, resource management and classic survival horror. Leon S. Kennedy returns as an experienced government agent, and his sections lean more heavily into high-intensity combat and action while still retaining horror and resource-management elements.

Both Grace and Leon can be played in first-person or third-person perspective, and Capcom allows the viewpoint to be changed according to the player's preference. This makes the same environments feel very different depending on how closely the camera is placed to the character.

Grace has unique survival systems. She can use a Blood Collector to obtain blood used for crafting ammunition and powerful items. In Standard (Classic) difficulty, Grace's manual saving uses Ink Ribbons at typewriters and autosaving is more limited, deliberately evoking older Resident Evil design.

Leon is more combat-capable. His toolkit includes firearms and a hatchet for close-range attacks and parrying. A well-timed Perfect Parry creates additional combat opportunities, while the hatchet can become blunt and temporarily limit defensive options.

The story reconnects the series with the Raccoon City Incident and its aftermath. The official premise centres on Grace and Leon confronting their respective pasts while uncovering a deeper truth connected to Raccoon City. The game includes ruined urban locations, medical facilities, hotel interiors and other environments designed around tension, exploration, combat and environmental storytelling.

Resident Evil Requiem supports amiibo. Grace Ashcroft and Leon S. Kennedy amiibo figures unlock exclusive weapon skins for compatible weapons in the game.

The Nintendo Switch 2 physical release is a Game-Key Card. The card acts as a license/key and the full game must be downloaded to the console before play. Once the software is installed, the core campaign itself is a single-player experience and does not require online multiplayer.

Capcom has continued supporting the game after launch. Photo Mode was added in a free update, followed by the free Leon Must Die Forever mode. The Deluxe Kit is separately sold paid DLC and includes costumes, screen filters, weapon skins, charms, an audio pack and additional files.

description_ar:
Resident Evil Requiem هي الجزء الرئيسي التاسع من سلسلة Resident Evil، وتجمع بين رعب البقاء الكلاسيكي والأكشن ضمن قصتين مترابطتين تقودهما Grace Ashcroft وLeon S. Kennedy.

Grace محللة في FBI تدخل تحقيقاً مرتبطاً بفندق مهجور وبماضي عائلتها، وتتميز فصولها بإحساس أكبر بالضعف والخوف وإدارة الموارد والاستكشاف. في المقابل يعود Leon S. Kennedy كعميل مخضرم، وتقدم فصوله قتالاً أسرع وأكثر عنفاً مع بقاء عناصر الرعب والذخيرة المحدودة وإدارة العتاد حاضرة.

تسمح Capcom بلعب قصتي Grace وLeon من منظور الشخص الأول أو الثالث، ويمكن تغيير المنظور حسب تفضيل اللاعب. منظور الشخص الأول يزيد القرب والتوتر، بينما يمنح منظور الشخص الثالث رؤية أوضح للشخصية والمساحة المحيطة.

تمتلك Grace أنظمة خاصة بها. يمكنها استخدام Blood Collector لجمع الدم واستخدامه في صناعة الذخيرة وبعض الأدوات القوية. وعند اختيار Standard (Classic)، تصبح الحفظات اليدوية لـGrace مرتبطة بـInk Ribbons والـTypewriters مع Autosave أكثر محدودية، في إشارة مباشرة إلى تصميم Resident Evil الكلاسيكي.

أما Leon فيملك أدوات قتال أقوى، ومنها الأسلحة النارية والـHatchet للقتال القريب. يمكن استخدام الفأس للـParry، ويمنح Perfect Parry في التوقيت الصحيح أفضلية في المواجهة. وقد يصبح الفأس Blunt بعد الاستخدام المكثف، ما يؤثر على قدرته الدفاعية حتى تتم معالجة الوضع.

القصة تعود إلى إرث Raccoon City Incident وآثاره. تتقاطع مسارات Grace وLeon مع حقائق من الماضي وأحداث مرتبطة بما حدث لمدينة Raccoon City، مع الحفاظ هنا على وصف خالٍ من حرق أحداث النهاية.

اللعبة فردية بالكامل ولا تحتوي Multiplayer تنافسياً أو تعاونياً. نسخة Nintendo Switch 2 الفيزيائية هي Game-Key Card؛ يجب إدخال البطاقة وتنزيل اللعبة الكاملة من الإنترنت قبل تشغيلها، وبعد تثبيت البيانات يمكن لعب الحملة الأساسية كلعبة فردية.

تدعم اللعبة amiibo. مجسم Grace Ashcroft ومجسم Leon S. Kennedy يفتح كل منهما Weapon Skin حصرياً للسلاح المتوافق داخل اللعبة.

بعد الإطلاق أضافت Capcom Photo Mode مجاناً، ثم أضافت Leon Must Die Forever كتحدٍ مجاني جديد. كما توجد Deluxe Kit مدفوعة تحتوي على أزياء وفلاتر وWeapon Skins وCharms وAudio Pack وملفات إضافية. وأكدت Capcom أن محتوى قصة إضافياً قيد التطوير، لكنه لم يصدر بعد ولا يوجد له موعد إطلاق معلن عند إعداد هذا الملف.

nintendoNotes:
Nintendo officially lists Resident Evil Requiem as Nintendo Switch 2 software released on 27 February 2026, with one player on one system, Action/Adventure categories, CAPCOM as publisher, amiibo compatibility, surround sound, HDR on compatible TVs, PEGI 18, and 28.7 GB download size.

Official Nintendo AU eShop language metadata lists Japanese, English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Russian, Korean, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Polish. Nintendo Europe condenses Chinese into a single "Chinese" entry.

There is a live regional metadata conflict regarding Save Data Cloud:
- Nintendo AU eShop currently displays Save Data Cloud as supported in its structured feature metadata.
- Nintendo UK/Europe explicitly states in the product's compatibility notice that this software does NOT support Nintendo Switch Online Save Data Cloud backup.
Because Save Data Cloud compatibility is normally game-level rather than region-specific, this file sets nintendo_cloud_save=false and follows Nintendo Europe's explicit compatibility statement, while preserving the AU conflict here for transparency.

The core campaign is single-player, so Nintendo Switch Online is not required to play the game itself.

The physical Nintendo Switch 2 release is a Game-Key Card. Nintendo's Game-Key Card documentation states that inserting a game-key card is followed by downloading the full game. Retail package photography for Resident Evil Requiem also explicitly identifies it as a Game-Key Card and indicates an approximately 30 GB download requirement.

NSUID 70010000101676 comes from Nintendo AU eShop. NSUID values can differ across regions.

Nintendo does not expose a reliable consumer-facing hexadecimal Title ID, and this research did not find an authoritative physical product-code catalogue entry strong enough to justify inserting a guessed code.

worldSummary:
Resident Evil Requiem returns the series to the shadow of the Raccoon City Incident. Rather than treating the 1998 catastrophe as distant history, the game builds its central mystery around people, places and consequences linked to that event.

Grace Ashcroft's investigation leads through oppressive interiors including an abandoned hotel and medical environments. Leon's path intersects with wider threats and ruined urban spaces, including the remnants associated with Raccoon City.

The world design follows classic Resident Evil principles: interconnected interiors, locked routes, keys and items, environmental clues, scarce resources, enemies that create pressure, and spaces that change in meaning as new tools or information become available.

This file deliberately avoids late-game location and story spoilers. The store description should communicate the Raccoon City connection, Grace's investigation and Leon's involvement without revealing the central mystery or ending.

perfNotes:
Nintendo officially confirms HDR on compatible TVs but does not publish fixed internal rendering resolutions or a frame-rate specification for Resident Evil Requiem.

Independent Digital Foundry technical coverage reports that the Nintendo Switch 2 version targets a 60 FPS experience using DLSS reconstruction. Reported figures are approximately:
- TV/docked: around 540p internal resolution reconstructed to a 1080p output.
- Handheld: around 360p internal resolution reconstructed to a 720p output.
- Frame rate: 60 FPS target, with drops possible in more demanding scenes.

The Switch 2 version retains the core visual identity and RTGI-style lighting approach while using platform-specific compromises. Exact internal resolution can change dynamically, so the values above are technical observations rather than fixed Nintendo-published specifications.
storageNotes:
Nintendo UK and Nintendo AU eShop list the digital game at 28.7 GB. Retail Game-Key Card packaging rounds the download requirement to approximately 30 GB.

Because the physical edition is a Game-Key Card, owning the box/card does not remove the storage requirement: the full game data must be downloaded to Nintendo Switch 2 storage.

A microSD Express card is not mandatory if sufficient internal storage is available, but it can be used to expand Nintendo Switch 2 game storage.

The Deluxe Kit and later update data require additional space beyond the base 28.7 GB.

faq.q: Is Resident Evil Requiem available on the original Nintendo Switch?
faq.a: No. The Nintendo version is released for Nintendo Switch 2.

faq.q: Is the game single-player or multiplayer?
faq.a: It is a single-player game with no co-op or competitive multiplayer modes.

faq.q: Does the physical Switch 2 version contain the full game on the card?
faq.a: No. The physical edition is a Game-Key Card and requires the game data to be downloaded to the console.

verdictSummary:
Resident Evil Requiem combines two different expressions of the series in one campaign. Grace Ashcroft provides slower, more vulnerable survival horror built around limited resources, exploration and pressure, while Leon S. Kennedy brings a more capable and aggressive combat style.

The ability to choose first-person or third-person perspective gives the campaign additional flexibility, while character-specific systems such as Grace's Blood Collector and Leon's hatchet/parry mechanics keep the two protagonists mechanically distinct.

The Nintendo Switch 2 port preserves the complete game but uses more aggressive reconstruction and technical compromises than more powerful platforms. The physical Game-Key Card requirement is also important for buyers because the retail card still requires a large full-game download.

studioAbout:
Resident Evil Requiem is developed and published by CAPCOM using the RE ENGINE, continuing the company's modern Resident Evil production pipeline.

The game is directed by Koshi Nakanishi, whose prior Resident Evil work includes Resident Evil 7 biohazard. The project deliberately combines different expressions of the series: Grace Ashcroft embodies a more vulnerable survival-horror experience, while Leon S. Kennedy enables a more experienced action-oriented style.

CAPCOM designed both playable characters around selectable first-person and third-person perspectives. The official manual documents character-specific mechanics such as Grace's Blood Collector and Leon's hatchet/parry system.

CAPCOM continues to support the title after launch through software updates, free modes and paid Deluxe content. As of the verification date, additional story content has been acknowledged as in development but has not been released.

CAPCOM's own RE.NET global statistics provide an unusually strong official playtime data point: the worldwide average first-playthrough completion time is 19 hours and 14 minutes.
